summary: First iteration full-stack testing of Paper & Loop. Backend: 28/28 pytest cases passed covering health, auth, admin guards, product filters/search/sort, cart CRUD + totals, wishlist toggle, order lifecycle (checkout → submit-payment → admin advance through all statuses → cancel path → stock restoration), admin product/settings/category CRUD, and analytics. Frontend: verified home hero+announcement, collections filter, PDP with room-preview toggle, add-to-cart drawer, demo login, wrong-password inline error text, admin login + admin sidebar/dashboard/products/settings, full checkout → GPay QR → txn submit → confirmation → order detail with animated timeline and Cancel button visible for payment_under_validation orders.

integration_issues.issue: Order rows on the admin orders LIST page do not seem to use the `order-row-<num>` data-testid convention (the customer-facing /account/orders uses it correctly). Found 0 elements matching [data-testid^='order-row-'] on /admin/orders even though the admin Dashboard 'Recent Orders' block clearly showed the orders. This blocks automated tests from navigating admin order detail and clicking `admin-advance-status`. Recommend adding data-testid="order-row-<order_number>" to rows in admin/Orders.jsx (matching the review_request contract).

action_items: Add data-testid="order-row-{order_number}" to rows in /app/frontend/src/pages/admin/Orders.jsx so admin order list is testable and consistent with customer side (as promised in the testids contract).

Optional: verify admin OrderDetail page renders the `admin-advance-status` button once row navigation works; behavior appears correct via backend (all 7 forward transitions succeed and payment_status flips to 'verified' on 'approved').
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~960 lines in one file — acceptable for MVP but consider splitting into routers/{auth,products,orders,admin}.py for maintainability.
`_next_order_number()` derives sequence from `count_documents({})`. If any order is ever deleted this will collide. Consider an atomic counters collection with $inc.
`get_optional_user` swallows all exceptions silently — fine for public endpoints but log at debug level for observability.
CORS uses `allow_credentials=True` with `allow_origins=['*']` — browsers reject this combo. If cookies are ever used, set an explicit origin.
MongoDB `_id` is properly stripped everywhere via projection/`strip_id` — good.
`update_product` uses `exclude_unset=True` but the frontend/admin may not pass partial payloads; not a bug, just note.

Order 'cancelled' via admin_update_status skips the forward-only ORDER_FLOW check — good — but does not append a timeline entry consistently vs customer cancel path (customer cancel adds explicit note). Minor UX inconsistency.
